scope: Operational guidance extracted from the user-provided VEDA — Slay the Spire 1 Player Manual. It is kept distinct from externally verified mechanics and does not authorize fixed strategy.

claims.statement: Treat map pathing as a graph of reachable nodes, not as a flat set of room icons.
claims.conditions: The visible connections and current position must be extracted with enough confidence before selecting a node.

claims.statement: Before an Elite, assess HP, immediate damage, defense, potions, plausible matchups, route aftermath, and alternatives rather than treating it as a normal fight.
claims.conditions: Requires a confident map-node classification and current run state.

claims.statement: At every combat turn, verify player state, every enemy identity/HP/intent/status, hand, and potions before choosing an action sequence.
claims.conditions: If a critical field remains uncertain, re-observe or require supervision instead of inventing it.

claims.statement: Evaluate combat as ordered legal actions with predicted intermediate states; do not evaluate a hand as an unordered collection of good cards.
claims.conditions: Re-observe after consequential actions or an unexpected transition.

claims.statement: Before investing in defense, calculate whether lethal is available; include HP, block, energy, modifiers, multi-hit behavior, and triggered effects.
claims.conditions: Only assert lethal when all relevant visible and verified mechanics have been accounted for.

claims.statement: Treat HP spending as a run-level tradeoff: accept damage only when it purchases meaningful tempo, safety, or future run strength.
claims.conditions: Compare damage taken, combat length, Burning Blood recovery, route, and future threats.

claims.statement: Card rewards are optional; add a card only when it solves a current or expected problem better than preserving draw consistency.
claims.conditions: Evaluate current deck, relics, HP, route, and known future threats; skipping is a legal strategic action.

claims.statement: Do not force a deck archetype early; build toward the problems this run actually presents.
claims.conditions: Emerging cards and relics can later justify a more specific direction.

claims.statement: When an unfamiliar card, relic, enemy, intent, potion, event, boss, status, or interaction matters, retrieve exact mechanics before inventing behavior.
claims.conditions: Use multiple reliable sources for externally verified mechanics where possible; retain disagreement in strategic advice.

claims.statement: Keep game facts, derived state facts, strategy, VEDA experience, and hypotheses distinct; a single run outcome does not prove a general rule.
claims.conditions: Future promotion of a hypothesis requires repeated evidence and an audit trail.
